passages.text: For the choirmaster. For Jeduthun. A Psalm of David.
passages.sermon: David wrote this psalm.\r\nHe gave it to the choirmaster.\r\nHe gave it for Jeduthun.

passages.text: I said, “I will watch my ways so that I will not sin with my tongue; I will guard my mouth with a muzzle as long as the wicked are present.”
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He gave it for Jeduthun.
David spoke these words.
He said, “I will watch my ways.
I do not want to sin with my tongue.
I will guard my mouth.
I will keep my mouth closed like a muzzle.
I will do this while the wicked stand before me.”
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ לִידִיתוּן מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃ אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֶֽשְׁמְרָ֣ה דְרָכַי֮ מֵחֲט֪וֹא בִלְשׁ֫וֹנִ֥י אֶשְׁמְרָ֥ה לְפִ֥י מַחְס֑וֹם בְּעֹ֖ד רָשָׁ֣ע לְנֶגְדִּֽי׃

passages.text: I was speechless and still; I remained silent, even from speaking good, and my sorrow was stirred.
passages.sermon:
David is the speaker.
David was completely silent.
David did not speak at all.
David did not even say anything good.
David’s sorrow grew stronger.
passages.original: נֶאֱלַ֣מְתִּי ד֭וּמִיָּה הֶחֱשֵׁ֣יתִי מִטּ֑וֹב וּכְאֵבִ֥י נֶעְכָּֽר׃

passages.text: My heart grew hot within me; as I mused, the fire burned. Then I spoke with my tongue: “Show me, O LORD, my end and the measure of my days. Let me know how fleeting my life is.
passages.sermon:
David is the speaker.
David is a psalmist and king.
David felt strong emotion inside himself.
His heart became hot within him.
He thought deeply about his situation.
As he thought, a fire burned inside him.
David spoke with his tongue.
He said, "LORD, show me my end."
He asked God to reveal the measure of his days.
He wanted to know how short his life is.
passages.original: חַם־ לִבִּ֨י׀ בְּקִרְבִּ֗י בַּהֲגִיגִ֥י תִבְעַר־ אֵ֑שׁ דִּ֝בַּ֗רְתִּי בִּלְשֽׁוֹנִי׃ הוֹדִ֘יעֵ֤נִי יְהוָ֨ה׀ קִצִּ֗י וּמִדַּ֣ת יָמַ֣י מַה־ הִ֑יא אֵ֝דְעָ֗ה מֶה־ חָדֵ֥ל אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: You, indeed, have made my days as handbreadths, and my lifetime as nothing before You. Truly each man at his best exists as but a breath. Selah Surely every man goes about like a phantom; surely he bustles in vain; he heaps up riches not knowing who will haul them away.
passages.sermon:
God, You made my days very short.
My life is like nothing when I stand before You.
Every person is only a breath, even at their best.
Every person walks like a shadow.
People rush about for nothing.
People gather wealth.
They do not know who will take it after them.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֤ה טְפָח֨וֹת׀ נָ֘תַ֤תָּה יָמַ֗י וְחֶלְדִּ֣י כְאַ֣יִן נֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ אַ֥ךְ כָּֽל־ הֶ֥בֶל כָּל־ אָ֝דָ֗ם נִצָּ֥ב סֶֽלָה׃ אַךְ־ בְּצֶ֤לֶם׀ יִֽתְהַלֶּךְ־ אִ֗ישׁ אַךְ־ הֶ֥בֶל יֶהֱמָי֑וּן יִ֝צְבֹּ֗ר וְֽלֹא־ יֵדַ֥ע מִי־ אֹסְפָֽם׃

passages.text: And now, O Lord, for what do I wait? My hope is in You.
passages.sermon: David speaks to the Lord.\r\nDavid asks, “What do I wait for now?”\r\nDavid says, “My hope is in You.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה מַה־ קִּוִּ֣יתִי אֲדֹנָ֑י תּ֝וֹחַלְתִּ֗י לְךָ֣ הִֽיא׃

passages.text: Deliver me from all my transgressions; do not make me the reproach of fools.
passages.sermon:
God, you see all my sins.
I have done wrong things.
Save me from every one of my sins.
Do not let foolish people shame me.
Do not let me become a disgrace to them.
passages.original: מִכָּל־ פְּשָׁעַ֥י הַצִּילֵ֑נִי חֶרְפַּ֥ת נָ֝בָ֗ל אַל־ תְּשִׂימֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: I have become mute; I do not open my mouth because of what You have done.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David says he has become silent.
David does not open his mouth.
God has caused these things to happen.
David remains silent because God has acted.
passages.original: נֶ֭אֱלַמְתִּי לֹ֣א אֶפְתַּח־ פִּ֑י כִּ֖י אַתָּ֣ה עָשִֽׂיתָ׃

passages.text: Remove Your scourge from me; I am perishing by the force of Your hand.
passages.sermon: David speaks to God.\r\nDavid asks God to remove His punishment from him.\r\nDavid says, "I am perishing because of the power of Your hand."
passages.original: הָסֵ֣ר מֵעָלַ֣י נִגְעֶ֑ךָ מִתִּגְרַ֥ת יָ֝דְךָ֗ אֲנִ֣י כָלִֽיתִי׃

passages.text: You discipline and correct a man for his iniquity, consuming like a moth what he holds dear; surely each man is but a vapor. Selah Hear my prayer, O LORD, and give ear to my cry for help; do not be deaf to my weeping. For I am a foreigner dwelling with You, a stranger like all my fathers.
passages.sermon:
God, You discipline a man for his sin.
You correct him because of his wrongdoing.
You destroy what he treasures.
You consume it like a moth eats cloth.
Every person is only a vapor.
O LORD, hear my prayer.
Listen to my cry for help.
Pay attention to my tears.
Do not ignore my weeping.
I am a foreigner living with You.
I am a stranger, just like all my ancestors.
passages.original: בְּֽתוֹכָ֘ח֤וֹת עַל־ עָוֺ֨ן׀ יִסַּ֬רְתָּ אִ֗ישׁ וַתֶּ֣מֶס כָּעָ֣שׁ חֲמוּד֑וֹ אַ֤ךְ הֶ֖בֶל כָּל־ אָדָ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃ שִֽׁמְעָ֥ה־ תְפִלָּתִ֨י׀ יְהוָ֡ה וְשַׁוְעָתִ֨י׀ הַאֲזִינָה֮ אֶֽל־ דִּמְעָתִ֗י אַֽל־ תֶּ֫חֱרַ֥שׁ כִּ֤י גֵ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י עִמָּ֑ךְ תּ֝וֹשָׁ֗ב כְּכָל־ אֲבוֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: Turn Your gaze away from me, that I may again be cheered before I depart and am no more.”
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David feels overwhelmed by God's attention and discipline.
David asks God to look away from him.
David wants relief from his suffering.
David hopes to find joy again.
David desires this joy before he dies.
David knows he will soon leave this life and be gone.
passages.original: הָשַׁ֣ע מִמֶּ֣נִּי וְאַבְלִ֑יגָה בְּטֶ֖רֶם אֵלֵ֣ךְ וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃
